scope: Implement and prove only the smallest standardized bounded lossless cross-harness handoff artifact/readback seam identified by the prior P3.17 qualification report. P3.1-P3.16 unmodified; Lean promotion state unchanged; P4 not started.
reuse_decisions: Active State Capsule (P3.1, working_set.py) is the full unmodified lossless payload -- no subset was hand-picked.

Content-addressed Artifact Store (artifacts.py) holds the payload; a new artifacts.parse_ref() helper was factored out and worker_protocol._artifact_ref now delegates to it (no duplicate ref-parsing logic).
Canonical JSON / stable_content_hash (contracts.py) used for every hash in the envelope, matching the existing WorkerTaskPacket/BrainPacket convention.
OMP (omp_adapter.py) and Hermes (hermes_adapter.py) adapters both call the same handoff.create_handoff_envelope/read_handoff_envelope -- no divergent per-harness logic.
brainctl handoff create/read CLI reuses the existing argparse/dispatch conventions (cli.py).
No new memory store, no new artifact store, no harness-specific format, no full transcript copy, no unbounded serialized context dump were created.
implementation_surfaces: src/second_brain/handoff.py (build_payload, create_handoff_envelope, read_handoff_envelope; legacy create_handoff/BrainHandoffArtifact preserved unchanged)
src/second_brain/artifacts.py (parse_ref helper, reused by worker_protocol and handoff)
src/second_brain/worker_protocol.py (_artifact_ref delegates to artifacts.parse_ref; no behavior change)
tests/test_handoff.py (new, 17 tests: losslessness, boundedness, 6 negative controls, cross-harness adapter parity)

fields: handoff_id (content hash of every other field -- self-evident alteration detection)
envelope_schema.payload: schema_version + full Active State Capsule dict + full requirement ledger, canonical-JSON-serialized and stored via artifacts.store_text (content-addressed, idempotent)

requirement_classification.evidence: contracts.BrainHandoffEnvelope; one schema, one validate()/from_dict(), used by both adapters and the CLI.

Envelope carries only identity/refs/hashes (1462 bytes measured); full capsule+requirements payload (61071 bytes) recoverable via payload_ref through the existing Artifact Store, never embedded in the envelope.

read_handoff_envelope validates schema/identity/hashes, resolves the payload artifact, and returns only bounded continuation-relevant state (objective, verification, decisions, next_action, requirement_summary).
handoff_id = content hash of every other field (self-evident tamper detection); capsule_sha256/payload_sha256/payload_canonical_sha256 independently verified structural + byte-exact recovery.
Dogfood: a second real OMP-primary session recovered the full continuation state via the Hermes adapter with only the 1462-byte envelope as input -- no source conversation history.

state/p3_17_dogfood/handoff-lifecycle-evidence.json: OMP-primary session 01a046da-9348-7009-aa30-035d615f774f created the envelope from this session's own live capsule; OMP-primary session 01a046dd-83e7-7330-8c47-5e259defa255 recovered it via `second_brain autoinject hermes-hook` (hermes_adapter.handle_request, event=handoff_read) with matching capsule_sha256, 234 verification keys, 40 decisions, 28 confirmed_facts.

tests/test_handoff.py::TestCrossHarnessAdapters proves both OMP-creates/Hermes-reads and Hermes-creates/OMP-reads using the identical envelope schema and functions; frozen contract does not mandate bidirectionality but it was proven anyway since the implementation is inherently symmetric.

payload_sha256 (raw artifact byte hash via artifacts.expand) and payload_canonical_sha256 (structural hash via stable_content_hash on the parsed payload) are computed through two independent code paths and both verified to match.
Real envelope 1462 bytes <= 8192-byte bound; payload 61071 bytes stays in the Artifact Store and is never counted as transported context.

365 estimated envelope tokens vs 15267 estimated payload tokens (41.77x); 59609 bytes avoided vs a naive full-payload-inline baseline. Provider-side cache/model counters were unavailable on this harness path and no cache savings are claimed.

tests/test_handoff.py proves HANDOFF_ID_MISMATCH (altered envelope), HANDOFF_HASH_MISMATCH (altered payload), HANDOFF_ARTIFACT_UNRESOLVED (missing artifact), HANDOFF_PROJECT_MISMATCH (wrong project), HANDOFF_STALE (+ explicit allow_stale classification), HANDOFF_SCHEMA_MISMATCH (unsupported schema), HANDOFF_MALFORMED (oversized ref lists rejected, not silently truncated).
unavailable_evidence is a distinct bounded field from evidence_refs; tests/test_handoff.py::test_unavailable_evidence_distinct_from_empty proves the distinction.
state/p3_17_dogfood/handoff-lifecycle-evidence.json -- IDs, hashes, refs, and bounded metrics only; no large payloads stored.

Full existing pytest suite (unchanged) passes 100%; git diff touches only artifacts.py, cli.py, contracts.py, handoff.py, hermes_adapter.py, omp_adapter.py, worker_protocol.py, and the new tests/test_handoff.py.
P3.1-P3.16 remain PROVEN; Lean remains candidate/HOLD_SHADOW; P4 not started.

verification.regression_tests: full pytest suite: 100% pass, unchanged from pre-P3.17 baseline
verification.static: ruff check: all checks passed on every touched file; pyright: 0 errors/0 warnings/0 informations

smallest_genuine_remaining_gap: none -- the standardized bounded lossless cross-harness handoff artifact/readback seam identified as the smallest missing P3.17 gap is closed and independently proven.
